newsitem.title: CANADA: Imasco drops further, rebound seen likely.
newsitem.headline: Imasco drops further, rebound seen likely.

text.p: Imasco Ltd shares tumbled further on Friday as the pressure continued on U.S.-based tobacco giant Philip Morris Cos Inc after an admission by another tobacco company that smoking is addictive.
"Imasco is Philip Morris-related but personally I think it's maybe overdone here," said one trader.
Imasco shares were down 2.20 at 34.75 in hectic trade of 1.39 million shares after dropping sharply on Thursday. The stock closed at 38.40 on March 17.
Philip Morris was down 4-1/8 at 111-3/4 early afternoon.
The fall in tobacco shares was sparked by a pact Liggett Group reached under which it will release sensitive documents to U.S. states suing the tobacco companies.
The documents could shed light on the knowledge and beliefs of executives at other tobacco companies about the health risks of smoking and whether they purposely marketed cigarettes at youth.

The tobacco firms swiftly got an order barring Liggett from relinquishing documents protected by attorney-client privilege. But attorneys general said if the documents show criminal activity, they would not be protected.
But analysts and traders said the impact on Imasco is probably exaggerated.
"It's not in the same jurisdiction. There are no Canadian related lawsuits. The stock at these levels is still attractive on a yield basis," the trader said.
He said Imasco is likely to rebound next week as investors realize that the selling is overdone.
"We are following the (Liggett) story closely. But for Imasco, these issues are far less important than for U.S. companies," said ScotiaMcLeod Inc consumer products analyst Steven Holt.
